scene_description: A compact tiled bedroom viewed from above, with a bed in the foreground, white shelving and a narrow cabinet against the back wall, two floor lamps, a door and a white furnishing at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial image has a dark vertical opening at the back but no prominent door leaf extending into the room. The bed and right-side furnishing remain unobstructed by a door.
candidate_target_observations: A large light-colored, two-panel door leaf now projects into the room from the back opening and overlaps the background and the bed's far edge. This reproduces the reference's prominent foreground door more closely, though its orientation, silhouette and placement differ: the reference leaf is angled with a diagonal lower edge, reaches farther downward, and is closer to the right foreground furnishing.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The candidate door appears as a coherent tall paneled slab, with a plausible projected overlap in the room, although its visible attachment and exact hinge relationship are not clear. The shelving, cabinet, lamps and bed retain broadly plausible simplified shapes. RGB views cannot establish mesh contact or hidden intersections.
new_visible_defects: The added door is more upright and front-facing than in the reference, with a different bottom silhouette and less rightward foreground occlusion. Its light, nearly uniform finish lacks the reference's visible wood grain.
other_changes: Apart from the door, the initial and current scenes appear essentially unchanged. Both use a simplified gray floor, muted neutral lighting and smooth white surfaces, unlike the reference's mottled floor, warmer wood door and stronger warm lamp illumination. The candidate camera shows a wider, lower framing of the bed and more of the back wall than the reference; the right furnishing also has a different silhouette.

evidence.description: Wood-grained door leaf extends diagonally into the foreground with a slanted lower edge.
Dark back opening is visible without a comparable foreground door leaf.
A tall pale paneled door now crosses the back of the room and occludes part of the bed edge, but is more front-facing than the reference leaf.
White shelves, narrow glass-front cabinet and floor lamps sit against tiled walls with warm illumination.
Corresponding simplified shelves, cabinet and lamps occupy a similar left and back arrangement, under flatter neutral light.
The foreground bed and right furnishing are simplified and the floor is uniformly gray.

uncertainty: The intended target is inferred from the visible door change; no separate target specification was provided. The images do not establish hinge attachment, actual contact, collisions, hidden geometry or long-term capability.
